visual.general_description: Grayscale axial head CT slice at lateral-ventricle level showing patchy hyperdense areas in the hemisphere on the right side of the image.
visual.detailed_description: Single unlettered axial CT image on a black background in a soft-tissue brain window. The skull is bright white, the lateral ventricles are dark and symmetric in position, and the midline falx runs from an anterior notch to a bright posterior midline density. A small very dark (air-like) oval lies at the anterior midline against the inner table. On the hemisphere shown on the right side of the image there are patchy bright (hyperdense) foci along the cortex and sulci, a brighter focus beside the posterior horn region, and brighter periventricular tissue next to the lateral ventricle; the left side of the image shows visible sulci and fewer bright patches. A band of soft-tissue thickening lies outside the skull on the right side of the image. Two white curved arcs lie at the left and right edges outside the head. A small "P" is at the bottom centre and a tiny low-contrast "R" (legible on magnification) sits at the left margin, so the image left is the patient's right; no patient name, number, date or scanner text is visible.
